generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, experiential learning runs through placements, practicals and research work. You might run a study, observe in a clinical setting, or facilitate a group, and the learning is not the activity itself but what you make of it afterwards. Psychologists are trained to treat experience as something to reflect on: a session that did not go to plan, or a participant who reacted unexpectedly, becomes material for understanding your own practice once you take it through the cycle.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students finish the same research placement and are asked what they learned from it.

Tom says the placement was useful and that he enjoyed collecting data and gained experience. That is a report of the experience, not learning from it. Tom has stopped at the experiencing mode: the placement happened, but it has not been reflected on, thought through, or turned into anything to carry forward. The experience sits as a memory, not as knowledge.

Amara says the placement showed her that she briefs participants better when she rehearses the standardised instructions first. One session where she improvised left a participant confused and the data unusable. She noticed what happened, worked out why, linked it to what she had read about standardisation, and named what she will do differently. Amara has moved through the whole cycle, transforming the experience into knowledge.

Both students had the same placement. Only Amara transformed it, which is what experiential learning means.
generatedProse.summary: Experiential learning in psychology is the creation of knowledge through the transformation of experience: a placement or practical alone is not the learning. Kolb's cycle names four modes, experiencing, reflecting, thinking and acting, and two dimensions beneath them, grasping and transforming experience. You can now explain the idea and describe the cycle. The next lesson uses it to structure a reflection on a real psychological experience.

check.body: In her reflection on the placement, Amara moved through Kolb's four modes. Which option lists them in the order this lesson gave?

feedback.correct: That's right. The four modes are experiencing, reflecting, thinking and acting.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Recall the mode Amara starts from, the concrete experience itself.
feedback.incorrectFinal: The four modes are experiencing, reflecting, thinking and acting. One option reorders them and one names a different model.
